claim: On 2025-08-04 SQS raised the maximum message payload size from 256 KiB to 1 MiB for standard and FIFO queues. The message quota page now lists a maximum of 1,048,576 bytes (1 MiB).
question: What is the maximum SQS message size now, and when did it change from 256 KiB?

qualifiers.scope: per message, standard and FIFO queues
qualifiers.condition: the What's New post says the change is available in all AWS commercial Regions and AWS GovCloud (US)

evidence.quote: The minimum message size is 1 byte (1 character). The maximum is 1,048,576 bytes (1 MiB).

Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) has increased the maximum message payload size from 256 KiB to 1 MiB, enabling customers to send and receive larger messages through their Amazon SQS standard and FIFO queues.
Posted on: Aug 4, 2025
evidence.heading: Amazon SQS increases maximum message payload size to 1 MiB

note: d108. Examinable (GA before 2026-07-15). Older questions and the SNS FAQ may still say 256 KB. The change feed (changes for sqs) has no row for this post; the post itself is a saved page. Current-truth numbers fact: sqs-message-size-range.

claim: On 2026-09-18 SNS added support for message payloads up to 1 MiB, a 4x increase from the previous 256 KiB limit. Topics still accept messages up to 256 KiB by default.
question: What is the default SNS message size, and what changed on 2026-09-18?

qualifiers.condition: not examinable yet: general availability on 2026-09-18 is after 2026-07-15; the 1 MiB size needs the MaximumMessageSize topic attribute; the General Reference quota page still lists a 256 KiB maximum

evidence.quote: By default, topics accept messages up to 256 KiB.
Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) now supports message payloads up to 1 MiB, a 4x increase from the previous 256 KiB limit, so you can publish larger messages to your SNS topics.

evidence.heading: Amazon SNS now supports message payloads up to 1 MiB

claim: On 2026-01-29 EventBridge increased the event payload size from 256 KB to 1 MB. The PutEvents page now says the total request size must be less than 1 MB (1,048,576 bytes). The announcement says the feature is available in all commercial Regions except Asia Pacific (New Zealand), Asia Pacific (Thailand), Asia Pacific (Malaysia), Asia Pacific (Taipei) and Mexico (Central).
question: What is the EventBridge event size limit now, and when did it change from 256 KB?

qualifiers.scope: per PutEvents request (sum of all entries)
qualifiers.condition: event buses; not available in five listed Regions

evidence.quote: The total request size—that is, the sum of all event entries in the request—must be less than 1 MB (1,048,576 bytes).

Amazon EventBridge increases event payload size from 256 KB to 1 MB, enabling developers to ingest richer, complex payloads for their event-driven workloads without the need to split, compress, or externalize data.
Posted on: Jan 29, 2026
evidence.heading: Announcing increased 1 MB payload size support in Amazon EventBridge

evidence.quote: This feature is available in all commercial AWS Regions where Amazon EventBridge is offered, except Asia Pacific (New Zealand), Asia Pacific (Thailand), Asia Pacific (Malaysia), Asia Pacific (Taipei), and Mexico (Central).

note: d110. Examinable (GA before 2026-07-15). The eb-quota page does not list the event size; eb-putevents is current truth. The same page says up to 10 event entries per PutEvents request while eb-quota lists 1 to 100 entries for the new bus only (numbers lens).

claim: In November 2024 SQS increased the in-flight limit for FIFO queues from 20K to 120K messages. The FIFO quota page now says FIFO queues support a maximum of 120,000 in-flight messages.
question: What is the in-flight message limit of an SQS FIFO queue, and what was it before November 2024?

qualifiers.condition: an increase beyond the limit can be requested from AWS Support

evidence.quote: FIFO queues support a maximum of 120,000 in-flight messages (messages received by a consumer but not yet deleted).
Amazon SQS increases the in-flight limit for FIFO queues from 20K to 120K messages.

note: d112. The What's New page itself is blocked by robots.txt; the quote is from the saved What's New feed (api/whats-new-v2-amazon-sqs). Current-truth numbers fact: sqs-in-flight-fifo-limit. Standard queues are approximately 120,000 in flight.

claim: The SQS console page says that on August 17, 2022, default server-side encryption (SSE) was applied to all SQS queues. The documentation history lists default SSE with SQS-owned encryption keys (SSE-SQS) on September 26, 2022. The default option applies only when you create a queue without specifying encryption attributes.
question: Are new SQS queues encrypted at rest by default, and since when?

values.display: default server-side encryption (SSE) was applied to all Amazon SQS queues

qualifiers.condition: the default option is only effective when you create a queue without specifying encryption attributes

evidence.quote: On August 17, 2022, default server-side encryption (SSE) was applied to all Amazon SQS queues.

| [Default server-side encryption (SSE) is available](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-getting-started.html#step-create-standard-queue) | Server-side encryption (SSE) using SQS-owned encryption (SSE-SQS) by default. | September 26, 2022 |
The default SSE option is only effective when you create a queue without specifying encryption attributes.

note: d113. Three dates in the sources: the creating-queue page says August 17, 2022; the documentation history row is September 26, 2022; the What's New post is dated 2022-10-04 (page blocked by robots.txt, feed row only). No saved page states the old value (queues not encrypted by default), so changed is null. Older questions may assume that encryption must be switched on.

claim: Fair queues support for standard queues was added on July 21, 2025. SQS applies the fairness capability automatically in all standard queues, for messages with the MessageGroupId property, and a standard queue message group ID does not enforce message ordering.
question: When were SQS fair queues added, and how do you use them on a standard queue?

qualifiers.condition: MessageGroupId on a standard queue is only a tenant identifier and does not enforce message ordering

evidence.quote: | [Fair Queues support](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-fair-queues.html) | Fair Queues support added for standard queues. | July 21, 2025 |
The fairness capability will be applied automatically in all Amazon SQS standard queues for messages with the MessageGroupId property.
On standard queues, MessageGroupId is used only as a tenant identifier for fair queues and does not enforce message ordering.

note: d115. Examinable (before 2026-07-15). Fair queues target the noisy-neighbor problem in multi-tenant queues.

claim: On 2025-11-13 EventBridge began to support SQS fair queues as targets. To route events to a fair queue, select it as a target of a rule and include a MessageGroupID parameter.
question: Can an EventBridge rule target an SQS fair queue, and what must you set?

qualifiers.condition: the post says support for fair queue and FIFO targets is available in all AWS commercial and AWS GovCloud (US) Regions

evidence.quote: Amazon EventBridge now supports Amazon SQS fair queues as targets, enabling you to build more responsive event-driven applications.
Be sure to include a MessageGroupID parameter, which can be specified with either a static value or JSON path expression.
Posted on: Nov 13, 2025
evidence.heading: Amazon EventBridge now supports targeting SQS fair queues

claim: In November 2023 SQS added dead-letter queue redrive for FIFO queues: customers can redrive messages from a FIFO dead-letter queue to FIFO source queues or FIFO custom destination queues. Before, SQS supported redriving only from a standard dead-letter queue to standard queues.
question: Can you redrive messages from a FIFO dead-letter queue, and since when?

values.display: from a FIFO dead-letter queue to FIFO source queues or FIFO custom destination queues

qualifiers.condition: the redrive destination must be the same queue type as the dead-letter queue

evidence.quote: Amazon SQS already supports redriving messages from a standard dead-letter queue to a standard source queues or a standard custom destination queue.
Now SQS customers can also redrive messages from a FIFO dead-letter queue to FIFO source queues or FIFO custom destination queues.
However, you can also configure any other queue as the redrive destination if both queues are the same type.

changed.was: redriving messages from a standard dead-letter queue to a standard source queues or a standard custom destination queue

note: d116. The What's New page is blocked by robots.txt; the quotes are from the saved What's New feed. The API redrive arrived on June 7, 2023 (sqs-change-dlq-redrive-api-2023); redrive in the console for standard queues came on November 10, 2021.
